title: A practice queue with independent state
prompt: Build a PracticeQueue class for a small interview workshop. Each queue must own its waiting list. add(name) appends a string to the queue and returns None. next() removes and returns the oldest name, or None if empty. waiting() returns a new list of the waiting names in order. Changing that returned list must not change the queue. Duplicate names are allowed. First explain where the mutable state belongs and trace two independent queues before implementing the methods.

examples.explanation: The oldest arrival leaves first; waiting() now returns ['Leo'].

examples.input: a = PracticeQueue(); b = PracticeQueue(); a.add('Maya'); b.waiting()
examples.explanation: Each instance has its own mutable state.

constraints: Names are strings; duplicates are valid.
An empty queue returns None from next().
waiting() returns a fresh list every time.
Use only the Python standard library. At most 100 waiting names.

baselineTests.name: Empty queue
baselineTests.code:
q = PracticeQueue()
assert q.waiting() == []
assert q.next() is None

baselineTests.name: Arrival order
baselineTests.code:
q = PracticeQueue()
assert q.add('Maya') is None
q.add('Leo')
assert q.next() == 'Maya'
assert q.waiting() == ['Leo']
assert q.next() == 'Leo'
assert q.next() is None

baselineTests.name: Independent instances
baselineTests.code:
a, b = PracticeQueue(), PracticeQueue()
a.add('Maya')
assert b.waiting() == []
b.add('Leo')
assert a.waiting() == ['Maya']
assert b.waiting() == ['Leo']

baselineTests.name: Returned list is independent
baselineTests.code:
q = PracticeQueue()
q.add('Maya')
view = q.waiting()
view.clear()
assert q.waiting() == ['Maya']
assert q.waiting() is not q.waiting()

baselineTests.name: Duplicate names
baselineTests.code:
q = PracticeQueue()
q.add('Maya')
q.add('Maya')
assert q.next() == 'Maya'
assert q.waiting() == ['Maya']

hints: A mutable attribute declared on the class is shared. Create the waiting container inside __init__ for each instance.
Use list(self._waiting) to return a snapshot. A collections.deque supports removing from the front without shifting every remaining name.
learningObjectives: Define a small, testable object interface.
Return defensive snapshots and reason about edge cases.
